faq.q: Why does hail fall in summer?
faq.a: Hail needs a thunderstorm with very strong rising air, and those form most on warm, humid days. High in the storm it is below freezing even in summer, and big stones fall too fast to melt.
asks: How can it hail when it is hot?

faq.a: Water that stays liquid below 0 degrees Celsius because it has nothing to freeze onto. In storm clouds it freezes instantly when it touches a hailstone.
asks: How can water be below freezing and still liquid?

faq.a: A hailstone passes through parts of the storm with different temperatures and amounts of water. Fast freezing traps air bubbles and makes cloudy ice, slow freezing makes clear ice, so it builds layers like an onion.
asks: Why is hail cloudy and clear inside?

faq.a: Most are pea sized, but strong storms make stones as big as golf balls or even grapefruit. The heaviest on record fell in Bangladesh in 1986 and weighed about one kilogram.

faq.q: What is the difference between hail and sleet?
faq.a: Hail is balls of ice built up inside thunderstorms, often in warm weather. Sleet is a winter thing: in some countries it means raindrops that freeze into small ice pellets as they fall, and in others a mix of rain and snow.
asks: Is hail the same as sleet?

facts: The heaviest hailstone on record, about 1 kilogram, fell in Gopalganj, Bangladesh, in 1986.
The largest hailstone measured in the United States fell in Vivian, South Dakota, in 2010 and was about 20 centimetres across.

quiz.say: What keeps a hailstone up in the cloud while it grows?
quiz.show: A growing hailstone is held up by…
quiz.why: Powerful rising air in a thunderstorm holds the stone up until it is too heavy, then it falls.

wrong.1: Lightning is electrical; it does not hold up ice.
wrong.2: Clouds have no magnetic forces strong enough to lift ice.
